title: V-ResQ — VR Rescue Robot Control System
summary: A research-oriented VR interface for remotely controlling a rescue robot through a distributed architecture.
problem: Rescue operators need a clear, responsive way to control a robot and understand its state while remaining outside hazardous environments.
role: Team member contributing to prototype development, system integration, testing plans, and technical documentation.
outcome: A functional research prototype and documented test plan covering communication, control stability, safety behavior, and participant considerations. Performance results are not claimed here.
objectives: Return live sensor feedback to the operator
Design safe fallback behavior when communication is interrupted
process: Integrated VR input, edge processing, and embedded motor control
lessons: Safety feedback and system status are central UX requirements when an interface controls physical hardware.
solution: The prototype combines a VR operator interface, distributed robot-control services, live telemetry, and explicit safety states so an operator can understand and control the remote system from one workflow.

title: Badminton Pose Analysis
summary: A web application that turns video or webcam pose data into understandable badminton-stroke feedback.
problem: Raw pose landmarks are difficult for players and coaches to interpret without a clear analysis workflow and visual feedback.
role: Designed and developed the analysis workflow, pose-processing modules, and web interface.
outcome: A working local application supporting video or webcam input, pose processing, stroke analysis, and a results dashboard.
objectives: Present actionable feedback through a readable dashboard
process: Iterated on feedback states and analysis presentation
lessons: Computer-vision output becomes useful only when uncertainty and movement feedback are translated into plain language.
solution: A local web workflow accepts video or webcam input, detects body landmarks, classifies stroke phases, and presents technique feedback in a readable dashboard instead of exposing raw landmark data.

title: Smart Rehab Leg & Arm
summary: A gamified rehabilitation prototype that maps force and range-of-motion data to real-time play feedback.
problem: Repetitive rehabilitation exercises can be difficult to understand and sustain without immediate, motivating feedback.
role: Team member contributing to the Unity prototype, sensor-driven interaction, interface feedback, and project documentation.
outcome: A functional prototype with a force gauge, angle display, score, repetitions, and an endless-runner interaction for arm or leg exercises.
objectives: Support both arm and leg exercise concepts
process: Mapped sensor readings to game input
Adjusted UI anchors and gameplay presentation
lessons: Gamification works best when scores remain secondary to understandable movement feedback.
solution: The Unity prototype maps sensor input to a simple runner-style activity while keeping force, angle, repetitions, and score visible as immediate exercise feedback.

title: Fashion E-commerce Website
summary: An end-to-end fashion shopping experience covering discovery, cart, checkout, accounts, and seller flows.
problem: A multi-role store needs consistent navigation and clear state across browsing, purchasing, and account management.
role: Designed and implemented the front-end flows and connected them to a Node.js and MySQL application structure.
outcome: A multi-page project covering product categories, product detail, cart, checkout, authentication, profile, seller, and order-success screens.
objectives: Keep product and checkout information readable
process: Connected user flows to server and database modules
lessons: Consistent product information and visible cart state reduce friction across a long purchase flow.
solution: The application uses a consistent catalog system, reusable product cards, persistent cart state, and dedicated customer and seller flows across a Node.js and MySQL-backed multi-page store.

title: VR Hospital & Dental Clinic Simulation
summary: A healthcare simulation exploring spatial navigation, interaction cues, environmental audio, and a structured VR journey.
problem: Users in VR need clear spatial guidance and interaction feedback without relying on conventional screen layouts.
role: Built and arranged the Unity XR environment, interactions, scene flow, audio, and completion state.
outcome: A navigable hospital and dental-clinic prototype with waiting areas, interactable objects, audio, and an end state.
process: Added XR interactions and audio cues
Iterated on navigation and completion flow
lessons: In spatial interfaces, placement, scale, and feedback replace many conventions of flat-screen UI.
solution: A structured Unity XR journey uses environmental landmarks, consistent interactable cues, audio, and an explicit end state to guide users through the hospital and dental-clinic space.

title: CountBall Mobile Game
summary: An Android ball-counting game with spawning, basket interaction, game-state management, and scene flow.
problem: A simple mobile game needs an immediately understandable loop, responsive interaction, and clear state changes.
role: Implemented the Unity gameplay scripts, scene flow, basket interaction, and Android build.

objectives: Package the project for Android testing
lessons: Small games benefit from strong feedback and predictable state transitions more than feature volume.
solution: The Unity game uses a compact start-to-play loop, physics-based ball spawning, basket interaction, scoring, and scene-state scripts packaged for Android testing.

title: BATHUB WHALE AR
summary: An image-target AR experience with interactive 3D objects, rotation controls, lighting adjustments, and a mobile menu.
problem: AR content needs discoverable controls and stable presentation around physical image targets.
role: Developed the Unity scenes, image-target setup, menu flow, object rotation, and lighting controls.

process: Connected the menu and AR scene

solution: The Unity and Vuforia build organizes image targets into separate scenes and pairs them with lightweight rotation, lighting, and menu controls for mobile use.

title: ภารกิจพิชิตชัก — Roblox Educational Game
summary: A school-based Roblox learning experience that uses missions, NPCs, and in-game UI to communicate seizure-response knowledge.
problem: Health-response guidance can be difficult to remember when presented only as static information.
role: Developed multiple Roblox Studio iterations containing the school environment, classroom, NPCs, interface elements, sound, and scripts.
outcome: Five distinct development files document iteration from early school prototypes to the final-titled experience. Exact gameplay rules remain to be confirmed in a full Studio playtest.
objectives: Use NPC and interface feedback to guide decisions
process: Built the school and classroom setting
lessons: Educational game UX must balance clarity, emotional tone, and player agency.
solution: A mission-based Roblox experience places guidance inside a familiar school scenario, using NPC dialogue, decision screens, environmental cues, and feedback to reinforce seizure-response knowledge.

title: AI Human Detection for Disaster Response
summary: A V-ResQ module for detecting people and classifying disaster-scene postures on an edge-computing target.
problem: A remote operator needs support identifying people and posture states in visually difficult environments.
role: Prepared the detection workflow, dataset structure, model experiments, and edge-deployment project files.
outcome: A documented prototype pipeline for posture classes including bent, kneeling, lying, sitting, and upright. No unverified accuracy metric is presented.
objectives: Prepare the pipeline for edge use
lessons: Model output should be treated as decision support and communicated with appropriate uncertainty.
solution: The module structures labeled posture data for YOLO training, validates predictions visually, and prepares an inference workflow intended for an edge-computing target.

title: ArUco Robot Tracking System
summary: An OpenCV-based marker system for observing robot position and movement from a camera feed.
problem: Robot movement tests need a repeatable visual reference for estimating position and direction.
role: Implemented marker generation, detection, tracking utilities, and server integration files.
outcome: A working project structure for generating markers and detecting them in the robot-testing workflow.
objectives: Share tracking information with the control workflow
process: Connected detection to the project server
lessons: Reliable tracking depends on camera placement, marker scale, and clear feedback when detection is lost.
solution: The project generates known ArUco markers, detects them through OpenCV, and exposes marker position and orientation data to the wider robot-testing workflow.

title: Nine Hall Sensor Detection System
summary: A nine-point magnetic sensing system with calibration and signal-stabilization logic for reliable detection.
problem: Raw magnetic sensor readings fluctuate and can create false triggers without filtering and state logic.
role: Developed and tested the embedded calibration, averaging, hysteresis, confirmation, and adaptive-baseline logic.
outcome: A structured embedded prototype designed to reduce noise and false triggers. No unverified accuracy figure is presented.
process: Introduced confirmation counters and adaptive behavior
lessons: Good physical-interaction UX often begins with stable, debounced sensor input.
solution: The embedded logic combines calibration, rolling averages, hysteresis, confirmation counters, and an adaptive baseline to convert unstable analog readings into predictable detection states.
missingImages: A top-down photo showing all 9 KY-035 sensor positions.
A serial-monitor screenshot showing calibrated sensor values and trigger states.
A short test sequence showing the magnet moving across the sensor grid.
contributions: Developed and tested the embedded calibration, averaging, hysteresis, confirmation, and adaptive-baseline logic.

title: 3D Product Modeling with Onshape
summary: A collection of product-form studies created through parametric sketching, lofts, extrusions, transformations, and part assembly.
problem: Physical product concepts need clear proportions, manufacturable geometry, and a documented progression from sketch to assembled form.
role: Created the CAD geometry and documented the modeling process through Onshape screenshots.
outcome: Verified screenshots show a multi-part product stand, a stylus-shaped device, and an assembled scissors model. A perfume-bottle claim is intentionally not made without direct evidence.
process: Built forms with loft and extrusion tools
lessons: A strong product model communicates both overall silhouette and how individual parts relate.
